root.claim: A single deterministic Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes outputs $\operatorname{bin}_{2n}(\operatorname{val}(x)\operatorname{val}(y))$ for every pair of $n$-bit inputs $x,y$ in worst-case time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ with $\kappa=2^{-182}$.
root.method: Build two fast tape procedures (address-chunk interchange and simultaneous butterfly layers) from fixed linear networks with a rank saving, use them inside Harvey and van der Hoeven's Gaussian-resampling reduction of the digit convolution to synthetic polynomial transforms over $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$, recover the integer coefficients exactly, and bound every row of a cost table by $p^{1-2\kappa}$ times $Tp=\Theta(n)$.

motivation.text: Transform-based multiplication scans $\Theta(n)$ bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ levels, so beating $n\log n$ requires saving on both data movement and butterfly arithmetic; the two tape procedures provide these savings and the reduction carries them into exact multiplication.

quote.quote: Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$. We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

root.salient: The bound beats $n\log n$ by a strict power of the logarithm in the very multitape model of Schönhage and Strassen's conjecture, yet the saving exponent $\kappa=2^{-182}$ is astronomically small.

children.claim: Two tape procedures save a power of their parameter: interchanging two disjoint $u$-bit address chunks of an array of volume $V$ costs $O(Vu^\tau)$, and the normalized butterfly $H_0$ on one selected bit of each of $D\le d$ address chunks of polynomial records costs $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$, with fixed $\tau,\lambda'<1$.
children.method: Derive each procedure from a fixed linear network that exchanges two banks and restores scratch values, run the network on $W$ role streams of volume $V/W$ with frames chosen so that every edge costs as many smaller recursive calls as its label-dimension change, and solve the volume-normalized recurrence using $s<Wm$.

motivation.text: Normalizing time by stream volume turns the recursion into $F(mf)\le(s/W)F(f)+O(\text{overhead})$; because the network needs only $s<Wm$ smaller calls on streams of $1/W$ the volume, each factor $m$ in the parameter costs a factor less than $m$, which is a power saving.

quote.quote: After dividing cost by volume, multiplying the parameter by $m$ increases the recursive contribution by $s/W<m$. This strict inequality is the source of the power saving.

children.salient: The whole saving rests on a strict but tiny deficit: the relative rank deficits are $339/22587335000000\approx1.5\cdot10^{-11}$ and $73/19906842167500\approx3.7\cdot10^{-12}$, yet any strict inequality $s<Wm$ gives a power saving.

children.claim: Each power is at most $1-2\kappa$ and any fixed power of $\log p$ is eventually at most $p^\kappa$, so the large-input bound is $O(Tp\,p^{1-\kappa})=O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa})$, and schoolbook multiplication below one fixed cutoff gives a single machine with worst-case time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ for every $n\ge1$.
